method: Independent static source/call-path review using engineering:code-review SKILL.md; no external services

evidence.topic: BFF bridge ordering and authenticated host projection
evidence.observed: BFF outer bridge validates session/current account and replaces Authorization with request-local signed token before identity and rate middleware; arbitrary identity headers do not create endpoint authority.

Three-hour issued/idle/absolute deadlines are checked without refresh extension; live existing JTI allowlist is atomically compare-and-expired at login; each browser authentication rechecks allowlist, exact password revision and current tenant/account/permissions. Logout/password change cannot restore a revoked JTI.

evidence.topic: CSRF, Origin, cookie parser and WebSocket
evidence.observed: All cookie methods other than GET/HEAD/OPTIONS require exact allowed Origin and synchronizer token. WebSocket Upgrade requires Origin. Fetch Metadata, duplicate cookies/headers and mixed cookie/Authorization are rejected; fresh password login uses its own Origin+Fetch Metadata policy.

EdDSA token lifetime is exactly bounded to 300 seconds; issuer/audience required with asymmetric activation; fixed local key ring and kid/window checks reject unknown keys and remote key selectors. Legacy HS verification uses the separate existing symmetric key. EdDSA /auth/me selects AuthService.authenticate rather than HS-only legacy introspection.

Final-path no-follow/nonblocking descriptor, regular-file/16KiB bound, private EUID and access bits, at most active+previous public keys, active/private-key match and full signing TTL window checks are present. No actual key files were read.

evidence.topic: Argon2 work bounds and bcrypt migration
evidence.observed: Argon2 parameters/password/encoded sizes are bounded. Blocking tasks retain semaphore permits through cancellation. Only a successful bcrypt match triggers Argon2 replacement under tenant/user/hash CAS without changing password revision.

nonblocking_notes.topic: Legacy bcrypt cost has no application-level upper cap
nonblocking_notes.impact: A pre-existing unusually expensive stored bcrypt hash can occupy a bounded password worker for a long time on login or password confirmation. Dependency bcrypt 0.17.1 accepts cost up to31; only Argon2 work parameters have an explicit application ceiling.
nonblocking_notes.why_not_critical: No request path reviewed allows an unauthenticated client to supply encoded hash/cost; the input comes from the trusted account database. Exploitation requires an already-present/imported high-cost hash or a separate database write capability. Current live hash costs were not queried.
nonblocking_notes.next_action: During the existing consolidated acceptance, assess aggregate legacy cost metadata without exposing hashes; define an explicit compatible maximum before changing accepted legacy credentials. Do not benchmark or execute a cost31 verification.
